audit.why: Chart is Aurora,Skill,Kled,Kled,Aurora,Kled,Kled in both layers and matches the packet levelChart at six of seven rows (packet has Kled at Level 1 and Skill at First item; the existing whys justify the page's reading — she has ranged poke at 1 and Kled spikes on Eclipse). Both layers agree with each other, so nothing is flipped.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora's Level 6 spike was attributed to a root and a 'W exile' that do not exist in her kit.
audit.why: Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s): 'leaps in a direction, releasing a shockwave that damages and slows any enemies it hits. Afterward, she creates an area that slows enemies within it and allows Aurora to teleport from one side of the area to the other.' No root, no exile. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion and rewrote its side to the rift-slow plus the cross.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, whys[4] and wants.foe[1] now state the real mechanic — the rift slows you inside it and she crosses it as you commit — and Level 6 stays hers, which that still supports.

audit.whatIsWrong: The escape was named as 'Twofold Hex' and as 'her E blink' in different places. Both are wrong: Twofold Hex is Q, a 900-range missile with a recast, and The Weirding (E) is a slow-and-hop-back. Her escape is Across the Veil (W), a 700-range leap that turns her invisible on landing, on a 22/21/20/19/18s cooldown. The passive was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Getting the slot wrong ruins the whole plan: a player baiting 'her E' is baiting a 15s ability while the 22s escape stays in her pocket. Spirit Abjuration (P) heals her from spirits exorcised by her spells and attacks, which is why a poke war refills her and Grievous Wounds decides long trades.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, whys[1], wants.foe[0] and dontsFull[1].d all now name Across the Veil with its 22s cooldown and describe Twofold Hex as the 9s poke; dontsFull[0].d states Spirit Abjuration's healing.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on the tracked ability.
audit.why: Across the Veil at 22s rank 1 is by far the longest and most punishable window in the lane; Twofold Hex is only 9s and is not worth waiting out.
audit.corrected: 22s and 9s now both on the page, with the advice keyed to the 22s one.

notes: Two fabrications killed here: Aurora has no root and no 'exile', and her escape is Across the Veil (W, 22s) not 'her E blink' or Twofold Hex. Several remaining fields (mid, late, early, whys[2], whys[5], spikes[0], spikes[2], wants.you[0..1]) still say 'E blink' or 'blink' generically; they were left alone rather than force a rewrite outside the length band on fields whose surrounding advice is still correct — a follow-up pass could retarget them to Across the Veil. Her R carries a derived 'hardCC' flag that Riot's text does not support (shockwave damages and slows; the area slows) — no stun or root claim was written. focus.text 'Aurora Twofold Hex' is 18 characters, under the applier's 25-char skip threshold, so it cannot be retargeted through a normal edit.
